To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
survival of both a Pseudomonas and a Rhizobium inoculant in an acidic soil is related to pH of the soil solution and to the concentrations of Al, Ca, and Mg ions in the solution.

the use of soil solutions for bacterial viability assessments can be an efficient alternative to the use of nonsterile soils and that low-level liming increases survival of root-colonizing pseudomonad and rhizobium strains in acidic soils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
survival of a genetically modified root-colonizing Pseudomonas and Rhizobial strain in an acidic soil, which was amended with lime.
the survival of a genetically modified root-colonizing Pseudomonas sp. and Rhizobial strain in acidic soils, and the effect of liming on this survival.
the survival of a genetically modified root-colonizing pseudomonad and rhizobium strain in an acidic soil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of soil solutions, rather then nonsterile soils for viability assessments, is an effective and efficient alternative.

the use of fluorescent probes to determine viability is a very good method for assessing survival of bacteria in soil and soil solutions, and that survival of the root-colonizing pseudomonad and rhizobium strains in soil and soil solution was positively correlated with soil and solution pH, and basic cation concentration, and negatively correlated with aluminum concentration.

the survival of a genetically modified root-colonizing Pseudomonas and Rhizobiam strain in a low pH soil is directly related to the soil pH, and that survival is negatively related to the soil solution Al and positively related to Ca and Mg concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
survival of both strains was related to soil solution pH, and the effect of pH was more pronounced for the pseudomonad than for the rhizobia.
survival of both bacterial strains is directly related to soil pH and basic cations (Ca and Mg) and inversely related to Al concentrations in the soil solution.

, in general, survival of both strains was negatively related to soil acidity-related factors, and that low-level liming of acidic soils could be a useful management tool in enhancing survival of beneficial root-associated bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
survival of root-colonizing pseudomonads and rhizobia in acidic soils can be enhanced through liming at low levels.
the survival of introduced beneficial bacteria can be improved by liming acidic soils to a pH of around 5.0.
the use of low levels of liming can be an effective strategy for maintaining threshold populations of inoculant microorganisms in the field.
